It looks impossible to draw, because it does not fit on a sheet without deforming. But there is a way of fitting the whole of it into a circle: the Poincaré disc. And since a shader paints any function of the plane, hyperbolic geometry can be seen, travelled and tiled in real time.

Henri Poincaré propuso el modelo del dis: Henri Poincaré proposed the disc model in the 1880s, studying differential equations, not drawings. In 1956, the Canadian geometer Donald Coxeter sent M. C. Escher a paper with a figure of a hyperbolic tiling of triangles. Escher did not understand the formulas, but he did understand the drawing, and out of it he created the Circle Limit series (1958-1960), with fish becoming infinitely small towards the edge. Coxeter later wrote that Escher had constructed the lines to millimetre accuracy, with no more help than compasses and intuition.
